---
title: 4 - GeoJSON layers
---

So far, your webmap displays a basemap and a WMS layer from a remote server. In this chapter, you will add two local vector datasets: forest reserves and national parks in Tanzania.

Unlike the WMS layer, these datasets will be stored in your project folder and loaded directly by OpenLayers as GeoJSON.

By the end of this chapter, you will have three thematic data layers in your webmap, in addition to the basemap.

## 4.1. Download the datasets

Create a folder called `data` inside your webmap project folder, i.e. `you-webmap-folder/my-app/data`.

We will use two more datasets from the [Climate Risk Database](https://crd.resilienceacademy.ac.tz/). Open the following dataset pages:

- [Tanzania Forest Reserves 2022](https://crd.resilienceacademy.ac.tz/catalogue/#/dataset/1108)
- [Tanzania National Parks and Conservation Areas 2023](https://crd.resilienceacademy.ac.tz/catalogue/#/dataset/1105)

For each dataset, Download --> Export Data --> **GeoJSON** format. Click and save the export. Depending on your browser, the exported data may open in a new tab rather than downloading automatically. If this happens, save the raw data to your computer. This can be done e.g. via a *Save*-button, or by right-clicking the raw data window and saving it to your device.

![Download data from Climate Risk Database](images/4-1_download-geojson.png)

Save the two files in the `/data` folder you created, and name them as

- `tanzania_forest_reserves_2022.json`
- `tanzania_national_parks_2023.json`

Use filenames that match the actual datasets you downloaded. If you choose different names, you will need to use those same names in the code later.

Your project folder should now contain a structure similar to this:

### Checkpoint

Make sure both files are saved in the correct folder. Open each file in your editor and check that it contains geographic data rather than an HTML error page or a download message.


## 4.2. Import the required OpenLayers modules

Next, we will tell OpenLayers how to read and display the local GeoJSON datasets.

Open `main.js`. At the top of the file, you will find the existing `import` statements. These load the OpenLayers modules that the application needs.

We need three additional modules:

- `VectorSource`, which loads and manages the vector data.
- `GeoJSON`, which reads the GeoJSON format.
- `VectorLayer`, which displays the vector features on the map.

Add the following imports alongside the existing imports:

```javascript
import Map from 'ol/Map.js';
import View from 'ol/View.js';
import ImageLayer from 'ol/layer/Image.js';
import TileLayer from 'ol/layer/Tile.js';
import ImageWMS from 'ol/source/ImageWMS.js';
import OSM from 'ol/source/OSM.js';

import VectorSource from 'ol/source/Vector';
import GeoJSON from 'ol/format/GeoJSON';
import VectorLayer from 'ol/layer/Vector';
```


## 4.3. Add the GeoJSON layers to the map

Find the `layers` array in `main.js`. It currently contains the basemap and the WMS layer.

We will add a `VectorLayer` for each of the two local datasets. Each vector layer uses a `VectorSource` to load its file and a `GeoJSON` format reader to interpret its contents.


### Add the GeoJSON layers

Insert the following blocks into the `layers` array, in the position specified in the instructions:

```javascript
new VectorLayer({
    source: new VectorSource({
      format: new GeoJSON(),
      url: './data/tanzania_forest_reserves_2022.json'
    })
  }),

  new VectorLayer({
    source: new VectorSource({
      format: new GeoJSON(),
      url: './data/tanzania_national_parks_2023.json'
    })
  }),
```

The file paths must match your folder structure and filenames. For example, `./data/example.json` refers to a file called `example.json` inside the `data` folder.

### Understand the layer order

The order of the layers in the array determines their drawing order. For this exercise, arrange the layers so that:

1. OpenStreetMap is at the bottom - *first in the list*
2. Forest reserves are displayed above the basemap.
3. National parks are displayed above the forest reserves.
4. The WMS layer is at the top. - *last in the list*

This order means that the WMS layer can cover parts of the local vector layers. Later, you will learn how to style layers and control their visibility to make the map easier to interpret.

Now, your layer list should look like this in the `main.js` file:

```javascript
const layers = [
  new TileLayer({
    source: new OSM(),
  }),

  new VectorLayer({
    source: new VectorSource({
      format: new GeoJSON(),
      url: './data/tanzania_forest_reserves_2022.json'
    })
  }),

  new VectorLayer({
    source: new VectorSource({
      format: new GeoJSON(),
      url: './data/tanzania_national_parks_2023.json'
    })
  }),

  new ImageLayer({
    extent: [3228700, -1381359, 4567834, -162868],
    source: new ImageWMS({
      url: 'https://crd.resilienceacademy.ac.tz/geoserver/wms',
      params: {
        'LAYERS': 'geonode:tanzania_international_conservation_areas_2026'
      },
      ratio: 1,
      serverType: 'geoserver',
    }),
  })
];

Save `main.js` and refresh the map.


### Checkpoint

Your map should now contain the basemap, the WMS layer and both local GeoJSON layers. Depending on the current styles and layer overlap, the local data may not yet be easy to distinguish. In the next chapter, you will improve the appearance of the vector layers.

If a dataset is missing, check the browser developer console and confirm that:

- The file exists in the `data` folder.
- The filename and path in the code match the actual file.
- The file contains valid GeoJSON.
- The required OpenLayers imports are present.

### 4.1. Download GeoJSON layers

First, add a folder called "data" in your webmap-working-folder/my-app/data.

Go to Climate Risk Database --> Datasets --> Search for Tanzania Forest reserves 2022 and Tanzania National parks and Conservation areas 2023.

https://crd.resilienceacademy.ac.tz/catalogue/#/dataset/1108
https://crd.resilienceacademy.ac.tz/catalogue/#/dataset/1105


Open the Tanzania Forest reserves 2023 dataset --> Download --> Export Data --> Format GeoJSON --> A raw .json formatted file should appear as a new tab in your browser (if it did not download automatically). Save the file to the newly created data folder inside your webmap working folder. Rename the “result.json” to tanzania_forest_reserves_2022.json”. Do the same for the tanzania national parks 2023 dataset. 



Note: Depending on the browser you are using, saving this .json file can work a bit differently. Might be that you can save the raw data file by right-clicking the browser window and Save with name... (or something else that allows you to browse a location for the saved result.json file), or there may be a Save button in the top-panel of your browser. Google will help you if you can not find a way to save the file!

### 4.2. Import packages

Now, you'll need some more OpenLayers packages to be installed. This is done easily by importing the packages you need in the beginning of the code in main.js

Import 1) import VectorSource from 'ol/source/Vector'; 2) import GeoJSON from 'ol/format/GeoJSON'; and 3) import VectorLayer from 'ol/layer/Vector';

These do not have to be in any particular order. However, in the final code you'll see we have grouped similar types of imports under one "title" to improve the readability.

### 4.3. Add the vector layers to map

Add these local layers to the webmap by adding them to the layers-list
const = layers [ xxx ]
For now, there are only OpenStreetMap and the WMS layer. 

We want the layers to be in the following order:
- OSM
- Forest reserves layer
- National parks layer
- Our WMS layer

Simply add a code block for both datasets in a similar manner to the correct order, inside the layers list:



[And here is a new Tile Layer]

Note that the url must point into the correct path where your data layer files are. ./data/[file name] assumes the data-folder is inside the my-app folder. That is why we don't need to define the whole path, but the dot is enough. Also, although the data files are .json extension, OL can read them as GeoJSONs, meaning that it can retreive the coordinate system and coordinate information from the files. Similarly, you can open .json files e.g. in QGIS as such, without changing them to .geojson extension. This change can however be done just by renaming the file in your folder and typing .geojson to replace .json.
